propositions.text: This is an application for judicial review of an IRCC Officer's decision dated October 14, 2022, refusing permanent residence as spouse.
propositions.quote: This is an application for judicial review of a decision of an immigration officer [Officer] of Immigration, Refugee, and Citizenship Canada [IRCC], dated October 14, 2022 [the Decision], in which the Officer refused the Applicant’s application for permanent residence as the spouse of his sponsor.

propositions.text: The Officer was not satisfied the marriage was genuine or not primarily for immigration purposes.
propositions.quote: The Officer was not satisfied that the marriage between the Applicant and his sponsor was genuine or that it was not entered into primarily for the purpose of acquiring permanent residence in Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The court states this is a judicial review of an IRCC Officer's refusal of permanent residence due to doubts about the marriage's genuineness and purpose.

propositions.text: The application is dismissed because the Applicant's arguments do not undermine the reasonableness of the Decision.
propositions.quote: this application is dismissed, because the Applicant’s arguments do not undermine the reasonableness of the Decision.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the application, finding the Applicant's arguments do not undermine the Decision's reasonableness.

propositions.text: Applicant is a Pakistani citizen who lived in South Africa from 2004 to 2019, married first wife, had a son who still lives there.
propositions.quote: The Applicant is a citizen of Pakistan. Prior to living in Canada, he lived in South Africa from 2004 until 2019, where he married his first wife, and the couple had a son. The Applicant’s son still lives in South Africa.

propositions.text: Applicant divorced first wife in October 2019, moved to US in January 2019, arrived in Canada June 2019.
propositions.quote: The Applicant divorced from his first wife in October of 2019. He moved from South Africa to the United States in January of 2019, and he arrived in Canada in June of 2019.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Applicant's background: Pakistani citizen, lived in South Africa, divorced, moved to US then Canada.

propositions.text: Applicant lives with second wife, a Canadian citizen; met in July 2019, lived together March 2021, married April 2022.
propositions.quote: The Applicant now lives with his second wife, who is a Canadian citizen by birth. The Applicant claims to have met his wife at a bus stop on his way to a party in Scarborough in July 2019. They began living together in March of 2021 and were married in April 2022.

propositions.text: Applicant applied for permanent residence under Spouse or Common-Law Partner class with wife as sponsor.
propositions.quote: The Applicant sought permanent resident status under the Spouse or Common-Law Partner in Canada Class, with his wife as sponsor [Sponsor].

paragraphs.summary: The court describes the Applicant's relationship with his Canadian wife and his application for permanent residence.

propositions.text: Couple attended IRCC interview to assess marriage genuineness under IRPA and Regulations.
propositions.quote: As a part of the application process, the couple attended an IRCC office for an interview to assess the bona fides of their marriage and determine whether they met the requirements of s. 12(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, SC 2001, c 27 and s. 124(a) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations, SOR/2002-227.

propositions.text: Applicant and Sponsor interviewed individually; IRCC followed up with phone calls; Officer denied applications.
propositions.quote: The Applicant and his Sponsor were interviewed individually, and IRCC followed up with phone calls. Subsequently, in the Decision that is the subject of this application for judicial review, the Officer denied the Applicant’s application for permanent residence and the Sponsor’s sponsorship application.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the couple was interviewed by IRCC and the Officer denied their applications.

propositions.text: Officer stated concerns after assessing application, documents, interview; primary concerns not resolved.
propositions.quote: Based on the assessment of your information, including your application, the supporting documentation, and the information you provided during the interview(s). I brought my concerns to the attention of the primary applicant and sponsor. I was not disabused of my primary concerns.

propositions.text: Officer not satisfied marriage genuine or not primarily for immigration; Applicant not family class member.
propositions.quote: Due to the nature of my primary concerns I am not satisfied that your marriage to your sponsor is genuine or that it was not entered into primarily for the purpose of acquiring permanent residence in Canada. Therefore, as per the Regulations, you are not considered to be a member of the family class.

paragraphs.summary: The Officer found concerns unresolved and was not satisfied the marriage was genuine or not for immigration purposes, denying family class status.

propositions.text: Officer noted inconsistencies: no lease with Applicant's name, cell phone payment inconsistencies, walking time inconsistency, smoking discrepancy, streaming services inconsistency, Facebook concerns.
propositions.quote: The Sponsor could not provide a residential lease with the Applicant’s name on it (although the Officer accepted the Sponsor’s explanation that, in order to avoid a rent increase based on his income, she did not advise her housing organization that the Applicant had moved in with her); There were inconsistencies surrounding the couple’s cell phone payment arrangements; There were inconsistencies in the Applicant’s answers as to how long it takes to walk to a local store from their home; The Applicant stated he quit smoking in early 2021, but the Sponsor was unaware that he had ever smoked; There were inconsistencies as to which which streaming services they used at home to watch TV shows and movies; and The Officer had concerns about the legitimacy of their Facebook page and associated friends’ accounts, as well as inconsistent explanations as to why the Facebook account was created.

paragraphs.summary: The Officer found multiple inconsistencies and concerns about the couple's evidence and social media.

propositions.text: Due to inconsistencies, Officer not satisfied marriage genuine or not for immigration purposes.
propositions.quote: As a result of these inconsistencies and concerns, the Officer was not satisfied that the Applicant and the Sponsor were in a genuine marriage and not one entered into for the purposes of immigration.

paragraphs.summary: The Officer concluded the marriage was not genuine due to inconsistencies and concerns.

propositions.text: Issue is whether the Decision is reasonable; parties agree standard of review is reasonableness per Vavilov.
propositions.quote: Based on a review of the parties’ submissions, the substantive issue raised for the Court’s determination is whether the Decision is reasonable. As suggested by that articulation of the issue, the parties agree (and I concur) that the applicable standard of review is reasonableness (Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) v Vavilov, 2019 SCC 65).

paragraphs.summary: The court identifies the issue as the reasonableness of the Decision, with parties agreeing on the reasonableness standard.

propositions.text: Applicant's solicitor filed motion to be removed as solicitor due to inability to contact Applicant; Respondent does not oppose.
propositions.quote: Also, on November 9, 2023, the Applicant’s solicitor filed a motion in writing under Rules 125(1) and 369 of the Federal Courts Rules, SOR/98-106, seeking to be removed as solicitor of record on the basis that, commencing in March 2023, he has been unable to contact the Applicant. The Respondent does not oppose this motion.

propositions.text: Judgment will address the removal motion as well as the judicial review application.
propositions.quote: My Judgment in this application will also address the removal motion.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the solicitor's removal motion due to lack of contact and will address it in the judgment.

propositions.text: Applicant's agent counsel appeared due to solicitor removal motion; relied on Applicant's Memorandum; Respondent made brief submissions; agent counsel replied briefly.
propositions.quote: At the hearing of this application for judicial review, because of the pending motion for removal as solicitor of record, the Applicant’s solicitor sent agent counsel to appear in his stead. On the merits of the application, agent counsel relied on the Applicant’s Memorandum of Argument by way of principal submissions, the Respondent made brief oral submissions, and agent counsel made brief submissions in reply.

paragraphs.summary: The court describes the hearing procedure with agent counsel appearing and submissions made.

propositions.text: Officer unreasonably drew adverse inference from Sponsor not adding Applicant to lease despite accepting her explanation.
propositions.quote: he submits that the Officer unreasonably drew an adverse inference against the genuineness of his marriage based on the Sponsor’s failure to adhere to her housing bylaws by notifying the housing co-op that the Applicant was residing with her. He notes that the Officer accepted the Sponsor’s explanation that she did not notify the co-op because she did not want her rent to increase. The Applicant argues that it was unreasonable for the Officer to accept that explanation but still maintain a concern related to the housing issue.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant argues the Officer unreasonably inferred against the marriage's genuineness from housing lease issues despite accepting the Sponsor's explanation.

propositions.text: Court agrees with Respondent that Applicant misunderstands Officer's reasoning; no negative inference drawn from housing issue.
propositions.quote: I agree with the Respondent that the Applicant’s argument is based on a misunderstanding of the Officer’s reasoning. The Officer did not draw a negative inference based on this evidence.

propositions.text: Officer's concern was insufficient evidence Applicant resided with Sponsor without being on lease.
propositions.quote: Rather, the remaining concern that the Officer expressed was that, in the absence of the Applicant having been added to the Sponsor’s lease, there was insufficient evidence demonstrating that he resided with the Sponsor.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Officer did not draw a negative inference but was concerned about insufficient evidence of residence without lease inclusion.

propositions.text: Applicant argues Officer erred identifying cell phone plan inconsistency; financial arrangements irrelevant to relationship validity.
propositions.quote: Next, the Applicant submits that the Officer erred in identifying an inconsistency related to the cell phone plans of the Applicant and the Sponsor where no such inconsistency existed. The Applicant argues that the Officer’s analysis is irrational, as the particular financial arrangements that that the couple adopted for paying their various cell phone bills does not suggest any invalidity in their relationship.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant argues the Officer wrongly found inconsistency in cell phone plans and that financial arrangements don't affect relationship validity.

propositions.text: Court agrees with Respondent that Applicant misunderstands Officer's analysis; inconsistency was between testimony and documentary evidence.
propositions.quote: Again, I agree with the Respondent that the Applicant’s argument misunderstands the Officer’s analysis. The inconsistency the Officer identified was between the testimony and the documentary evidence submitted.

propositions.text: Applicant testified paying Sponsor's Chatr phone bill but no bank records show Chatr transactions.
propositions.quote: The oral evidence was that the Applicant paid the Sponsor’s phone bill with Chatr, but there were no records of Chatr transactions in the Applicant’s bank accounts consistent with this testimony.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Officer reasonably identified inconsistency between testimony and bank records about phone bill payments.

propositions.text: Applicant admits Facebook page was fake but says he was forthright, created it on counsel's advice, no inconsistency supports relationship invalidity.
propositions.quote: In relation to the couple’s Facebook page, which the Applicant admits was fake, he submits that he was forthright about the fact that the Facebook profile was created for purposes of his permanent residence application, because he believed based on his counsel’s advice that this was a requirement of the sponsorship program. He argues that there was no inconsistency in the Facebook evidence that would support a conclusion that the relationship is not genuine.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant admits the Facebook page was fake but argues he was honest and it does not show the relationship is not genuine.

propositions.text: Court finds Officer's analysis reasonable; fake Facebook profile and inconsistent explanations raise concerns about relationship genuineness.
propositions.quote: I have no difficulty concluding that this portion of the Officer’s analysis was reasonable. In addition to the concerns that would obviously arise from the creation of a fake couple’s profile on Facebook for purposes of supporting an immigration application, the Applicant gave inconsistent evidence as to the reason the profile was created. He first attempted to support the legitimacy of the profile and only later explained that the profile was created on the advice of his counsel.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Officer reasonably relied on the fake Facebook profile and inconsistent explanations to question the relationship's genuineness.

propositions.text: Applicant argues Officer erred relying on inconsistency in walking time to drugstore; difference is small and irrelevant to relationship genuineness.
propositions.quote: Next, the Applicant argues that the Officer erred in relying on the inconsistency between the Applicant’s evidence as to how long it took to walk home from a nearby drugstore and the evidence of the length of that walk based on Google Maps. The Applicant reported a 15 to 20 minute trip, when it was actually a 7 minute trip. He submits that the fact that his evidence was two or three times that of Google Maps does not translate into a significant inconsistency, given that the number of minutes involved is small. The Applicant also argues that this discrepancy is not relevant to the genuineness of the relationship.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant argues the walking time inconsistency is minor and irrelevant to the relationship's genuineness.

propositions.text: Court accepts walking time inconsistency is less significant but Officer could rely on it with other inconsistencies to question residence.
propositions.quote: I accept the submission that this inconsistency is not as significant as others upon which the Officer relies. However, it was open to the Officer to rely on this inconsistency, particularly when combined with the other inconsistencies identified in the Decision. I also have no difficulty understanding the Officer’s reasoning, i.e. that the Applicant’s inability to accurately identify the distance to the local drugstore raises concern that he does not actually live with the Sponsor.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the walking time inconsistency less significant but reasonably relied on with other concerns to question residence.

propositions.text: Applicant submits Officer unreasonably concluded relationship not genuine based on smoking evidence and failure to identify Netflix.
propositions.quote: The Applicant submits that the Officer drew unreasonable conclusions about the genuineness of the relationship based on the evidence surrounding his smoking and his failure to identify Netflix as the couple’s streaming service of choice.

propositions.text: Applicant testified he hid smoking from Sponsor; argues secrets do not mean relationship is not genuine.
propositions.quote: The Applicant testified that he was a smoker when the couple first started dating, but the Sponsor denied any knowledge of that. The Applicant testified that he hid his smoking habit from her. The Officer did not accept this explanation, reasoning that it would not be possible to hide from the Sponsor the smells and physical signs that would have resulted from his smoking. The Applicant submits that the fact that the couple has secrets does not mean that the relationship is not genuine.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant argues the Officer unreasonably relied on smoking and streaming service evidence and that secrets do not negate relationship genuineness.

propositions.text: Officer's analysis was about inconsistent evidence, not secrets, and rejected applicant's explanation about smoking secrecy as unreasonable
propositions.quote: I do not read the Officer’s analysis as based on the fact that there were secrets. Rather, the Officer was concerned about the couple’s inconsistent evidence and did not consider the Applicant’s explanation, that he kept his smoking secret from his wife, to be a reasonable one.

propositions.text: Applicant argues Officer did not rely on evidence to support analysis about smoking secrecy
propositions.quote: The Applicant argues that the Officer did not rely on any evidence to support this analysis.

propositions.text: Applicant suggests Officer required expert evidence that smoking leaves smell on body and clothing
propositions.quote: To the extent the Applicant is suggesting that the Officer required some sort of expert evidence to the effect that smoking leaves a smell on one’s body and clothing, I find that argument without merit.

propositions.text: Court finds applicant's argument about expert evidence requirement without merit
propositions.quote: I find that argument without merit.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Officer's concern was inconsistent evidence, rejects applicant's argument about lack of evidence and expert evidence requirement as without merit.

propositions.text: Applicant submits Officer's reasons ignore heteronormative cultural expectations about streaming service identification
propositions.quote: With respect to the streaming services, the Applicant submits that the Officer’s reasons are ignorant of heteronormative cultural expectations embedded in the conclusion about the Applicant’s failure to identify the correct streaming service.

propositions.text: Applicant provides little expansion on this submission
propositions.quote: The Applicant has provided little expansion upon this submission, and I do not find it compelling.

propositions.text: Officer found it hard to believe applicant did not recognize Netflix as principal streaming service due to its visibility
propositions.quote: The Officer found it hard to believe that the Applicant had not recognized that they use Netflix as their principal streaming service, as the name and logo is visible everywhere on the website and app.

propositions.text: Applicant has not convinced court of cultural insensitivity in Officer's analysis
propositions.quote: The Applicant has not convinced me that there is any cultural insensitivity embedded in that analysis.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues Officer ignored cultural expectations on streaming service; court finds no cultural insensitivity and finds Officer's disbelief reasonable.

propositions.text: Applicant argues Officer did not provide adequate reasons to conclude marriage is not genuine
propositions.quote: Finally, the Applicant argues that the Officer did not provide adequate reasons to support a conclusion that the marriage is not genuine.

propositions.text: Applicant submits Officer was obliged to consider totality of evidence including positive factors of genuine marriage
propositions.quote: He submits that the Officer was obliged to consider the totality of the evidence, including weighing any positive factors indicative of a genuine marriage.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues Officer failed to provide adequate reasons and consider all evidence for genuine marriage conclusion.

propositions.text: Applicant cites jurisprudence on balance of probabilities standard but no authorities supporting his position
propositions.quote: Other than citing jurisprudence identifying the nature of the balance of probabilities standard of proof in civil matters, the Applicant has not advanced any authorities in support of his position.

propositions.text: Applicant has not pointed to any evidence Officer overlooked
propositions.quote: Nor has he pointed to any particular evidence that he argues the Officer overlooked.

propositions.text: Decision explains Officer's concerns leading to conclusion marriage not genuine and not for immigration purposes
propositions.quote: I find that the Decision intelligibly explains the Officer’s concerns, which resulted in the Officer not being satisfied that this matter involved a genuine marriage and not one entered into for the purposes of immigration.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant cites balance of probabilities but no supporting authorities or overlooked evidence; court finds Decision adequately explains Officer's concerns.

propositions.text: Applicant's arguments do not undermine reasonableness of Decision; judicial review dismissed
propositions.quote: Having considered the Applicant’s arguments and finding that they do not undermine the reasonableness of the Decision, this application for judicial review must be dismissed.

propositions.text: No question for certification for appeal proposed or stated
propositions.quote: Neither party proposed any question for certification for appeal, and none is stated.

paragraphs.summary: Court dismisses judicial review as applicant's arguments fail; no appeal question certified or proposed.

propositions.text: Court advised parties it would grant motion to remove solicitor of record due to breakdown in communication
propositions.quote: At the hearing of this application, I advised the parties that, while my decision on the merits of the application was reserved, I was prepared to grant the motion for removal of the solicitor of record and that my Judgment would so provide.

propositions.text: Applicant's solicitor's motion materials show breakdown of communication and solicitor-client relationship
propositions.quote: The Applicant’s solicitor’s motion materials establish that there has been a breakdown of communication with the Applicant and therefore a breakdown of the solicitor-client relationship, such that the solicitor’s removal from the record is warranted.

propositions.text: Solicitor's removal from record is warranted
propositions.quote: such that the solicitor’s removal from the record is warranted.

paragraphs.summary: Court decides to grant solicitor removal motion due to breakdown in communication and solicitor-client relationship.

propositions.text: Agent counsel advised court to use their office address for service of decision on applicant
propositions.quote: Agent counsel advised that my Judgment could reflect their office’s address, which was provided to the Court at the hearing, for purposes of service of this decision upon the Applicant.

propositions.text: Judgment dismisses judicial review, denies appeal certification, grants solicitor removal, and orders service to agent's office address
propositions.quote: THIS COURT’S JUDGMENT is that: This application for judicial review is dismissed. No question is certified for appeal. The Applicant’s solicitor’s motion dated November 9, 2023, is granted and the Applicant’s solicitor is removed from the record in this matter. For purposes of service upon the Applicant, this Judgment shall be sent to 150 Carleton St., Suite 100, Toronto, ON, M5A 2K1.

paragraphs.summary: Court orders judgment dismissing review, denying appeal, removing solicitor, and service to agent's office address.
